paper_title: Black hole superradiance of self-interacting scalar fields
suggested_experiment_name: Black hole superradiance spin-down (X-ray binaries: Cyg X-1, GRS 1915+105, M33, GRO J1655-40, LMC X-1)
coupling_convention: GeV/f exactly as plotted on the y-axis (dimensionless ratio 1 GeV / f_a, i.e. inverse axion decay constant in GeV^-1 times GeV); x values are the boson mass mu in eV as plotted. To obtain f_a in GeV, take 1/(emitted value).
notes: Theory paper analyzing spin-0 BH superradiance with quartic self-interactions (lambda = mu^2/f^2). Main results are on the m_a vs f plane (Fig. 3, Fig. 10): BH spin-down constraints from spin measurements apply for large f but are evaded for f <~ 1e12-1e13 GeV where self-interactions saturate the cloud. Text states axion masses ~3e-13 to ~2e-12 eV would yield >10 LIGO CW signals for gravitational-strength interactions, and that 'much of the axion mass range is excluded for large f by BH spin measurements... these constraints do not apply for f <~ 1e12-1e13 GeV'. Data points are a rough encoding of this text-based boundary (masses ~3e-13 to 2e-12 eV excluded for f >~ 1e13 GeV); the actual exclusion boundary is only presented in figures (Fig. 3/10) with complex mass- and BH-dependent shape, so numerical values are unreliable. Paper also contains sensitivity PROJECTIONS for axion-nucleon (CASPEr-Wind) and gravitational-wave searches, but those depend on additional couplings (C_N) and are not simple coupling-vs-mass limits.
